events.title: Mukden Incident
events.description: Japanese military officers staged an explosion on the South Manchuria Railway near Mukden (present-day Shenyang) and blamed Chinese dissidents, using it as a pretext to invade Manchuria.
events.significance: The incident led to Japan's occupation of Manchuria and the creation of the puppet state of Manchukuo, exposing the weakness of the League of Nations and marking a key step toward World War II in Asia.

events.title: George Washington Lays the Cornerstone of the U.S. Capitol
events.description: President George Washington presided over a Masonic ceremony laying the cornerstone of the United States Capitol building in the new federal capital city of Washington, D.C.
events.significance: The Capitol became the enduring symbol of American representative democracy and the seat of the U.S. Congress.

events.title: U.S. Air Force Established and CIA Created
events.description: The National Security Act of 1947 took effect, formally establishing the United States Air Force as a separate military branch, and the Central Intelligence Agency was created.
events.significance: These institutions reshaped American national security structure and became central to U.S. strategy throughout the Cold War.

events.title: Death of UN Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjöld
events.description: Dag Hammarskjöld died when his plane crashed near Ndola, Northern Rhodesia (now Zambia), while he was traveling to negotiate a ceasefire in the Congo Crisis.
events.significance: His death was a major blow to the United Nations and remains the subject of investigations and speculation about possible sabotage. He was posthumously awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

events.title: First Publication of The New York Times
events.description: The newspaper was founded by Henry Jarvis Raymond and George Jones and first published as the New-York Daily Times.
events.significance: It grew into one of the most influential and respected newspapers in the world, shaping American journalism and public discourse.
